title: Generalisation
prompt: A bike rental model has a small training error and a much larger error on held-out rentals from the same population. What does the gap suggest, and how would you estimate performance on new rentals?
objective: Explain generalisation and interpret a gap between training and held-out performance.
expected_scope: Define generalisation, interpret the gap and describe an appropriate evaluation split.
hint: Which rentals has the model already had the chance to learn from?
reference_explanation: Generalisation is how well the model predicts new examples from the intended population. A much larger held-out error suggests the model may fit details that do not carry over from training. Evaluate on examples held out from fitting and tuning, using a split that reflects how the model will be used. Training error measures fit to known examples.

criteria.description: Defines generalisation as performance on unseen examples from the intended population.
Recognises that low training and higher held-out error suggests overfitting.
Evaluates on data held out from fitting and tuning.

critical_misconceptions: Treating the training error as sufficient evidence of performance on new examples.
